rationale: Anytype documents a localhost API bundled with the desktop app, a CLI that runs Anytype as a headless server, an official MCP server, and an agents skill that lets assistants like Claude Code read, search, and modify Objects. A versioned OpenAPI spec covers querying and updating objects, so agents can both read and write notes without the GUI. The 404 probe on doc.anytype.io paths does not contradict this, since the spec is published on developers.anytype.io. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration that headless read/write works in practice; API v2 is still pre-release with no published deprecation policy.

A probe confirms a live llms.txt at doc.anytype.io (HTTP 200) that indexes the docs as raw .md pages, so an agent can be pointed straight at it. Further agent-oriented material includes an AGENTS.md in the repo, an Anytype Agents Skill doc for Claude Code, Cursor and similar tools, and a machine-readable OpenAPI v2 spec 'built for agents and humans.' Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of agents actually consuming these docs, and no evidence of an llms-full.txt or an llms.txt on the developer portal.

The evidence shows no built-in, in-product AI that generates insights or suggestions from the user's data. The AI-related items describe external assistants (Claude Code, Cursor, and others) reaching Anytype data through the MCP server, Agents Skill, or local API. Those are external tools and developer building blocks, not an in-app capability. Queries and the Graph are deterministic organization features, not AI-generated insights.

Anytype documents no native automation feature such as triggers, scheduled jobs, or rules that run autonomously in the background. What the evidence does show are developer building blocks: a headless CLI server and a local API for scripting, plus an MCP server and an agents skill that external tools like Claude Code use to run scripts. Auto-updating Queries and background sync are adjacent features, not user-configured automations.

The evidence shows only ways for external AI tools to reach Anytype: a local API, an official MCP server, and an agents skill dropped into Claude Code, Cursor, or similar tools. These are integration building blocks, not a built-in assistant that users delegate tasks to inside the app. The GitHub mention of AI "Agents" (see AGENTS.md) does not describe an in-app assistant, and no other evidence documents one.

The headless server exposes the documented, versioned local API with a published OpenAPI spec, which scripts and agents can drive programmatically (anytype-docs-1, anytype-supp-openapi-v2, anytype-docs-5). The headless capability rests on a single short announcement, with no setup detail shown. missing for 10: detailed CLI/headless setup documentation, explicit CI usage guidance or examples (e.g., auth/key provisioning in pipelines), independent or hands-on corroboration of headless operation.

The evidence shows only the server direction: an official Anytype MCP Server and an agents skill that let external AI tools such as Claude Code or Cursor read and modify Anytype data. Nothing shows Anytype itself acting as an MCP client that connects to third-party MCP servers and uses their tools. Server-side and API capabilities belong to a different story and earn no credit here. Since a knowledge app with AI features could plausibly offer MCP client support, the axis applies, so absence of evidence is 'none' rather than 'na'.

Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of connecting an agent, and detail in the pack on setup steps, transport and the tools the server exposes.
